title: Class Sheet — PPCM & PGCD
intro: **PPCM** = smallest number they all share as a multiple (“meet again”). **PGCD** = biggest number that divides them all (“share equally”). Prime factors do both jobs.

hints: List the first multiples of 48: 48, 96, 144 … which one is also in the 36 table?
Or use primes: 36 = 2² × 3² and 48 = 2⁴ × 3. For the PPCM keep the BIGGEST power of every prime.

traps.0: 12 is the PGCD (the biggest number that divides both). The PPCM is a multiple of both.
traps.1: 72 is a multiple of 36, but 72 ÷ 48 = 1.5 — 48 doesn't fit in it.
traps.3: 36 × 48 is a common multiple, but not the smallest: the shared factors are counted twice.

solution: PPCM: biggest power of each prime → 2⁴ × 3² = 16 × 9 = **144**

hints: Which numbers divide BOTH 36 and 48? Find the biggest.
36 = 2² × 3² and 48 = 2⁴ × 3. For the PGCD keep only the primes they SHARE, with the SMALLEST power.

traps.0: 6 divides both, but it isn't the greatest — 12 does too.
traps.2: 24 divides 48, but 36 ÷ 24 is not a whole number.
traps.3: 144 is the PPCM (a common multiple), not the PGCD.

hints: You found both numbers in the last two questions: 144 and 12.
“×” means multiply.
Look at 36 × 48 — what do you notice?

traps.2: 144 is only the PPCM — don't forget to multiply by the PGCD.
traps.3: 12 is only the PGCD — multiply it by the PPCM.

solution: And 36 × 48 = 1728 too! For two numbers: **PPCM × PGCD = the two numbers multiplied.**
questions.idea: For TWO numbers: PPCM × PGCD = a × b (a great way to check!).

hints: Does any number bigger than 1 divide both 11 and 12?
11 is prime. Does 11 divide 12?
If the PGCD is 1, then PPCM = 11 × 12.

traps.1: You swapped them. The PGCD can never be bigger than the numbers.
traps.2: A PGCD must divide BOTH numbers — 11 doesn't divide 12.
traps.3: 23 = 11 + 12. The PPCM is a product, not a sum.

solution: Consecutive numbers share no prime factor, so PGCD = **1**.
questions.idea: Consecutive numbers: PGCD = 1 and PPCM = their product.

hints: Two different primes: what can divide both?
Only 1. So the PGCD is 1.
Then PPCM = 7 × 11.

traps.0: Swapped: the PGCD is the small one (it divides both).
traps.3: 18 = 7 + 11. The PPCM is a product, not a sum.

questions.idea: Two different primes: PGCD = 1, PPCM = their product.

hints: Use primes (or the divide-down ladder). 72 = 2³ × 3², 80 = 2⁴ × 5, 180 = 2² × 3² × 5.
Biggest power of each prime: 2 → 2⁴, 3 → 3², 5 → 5.

traps.0: 4 is the PGCD of the three numbers. The PPCM is a common multiple.
traps.1: 360 works for 72 and 180, but 360 ÷ 80 = 4.5 — it isn't a multiple of 80.
traps.3: 1440 is a common multiple (twice the answer), but not the smallest.

questions.idea: Three numbers? Same rule: every prime, highest power.

hints: A prime must divide ALL THREE to count. 48 = 2⁴ × 3, 60 = 2² × 3 × 5, 90 = 2 × 3² × 5.
Shared by all three: 2 (smallest power 2¹) and 3 (smallest power 3¹). 5 is missing from 48.

traps.0: 3 divides all three, but it's not the greatest — 6 does too.
traps.2: 12 divides 48 and 60, but 90 ÷ 12 = 7.5. It must divide ALL three.
traps.3: 720 is the PPCM of these three numbers.

solution: Shared by all three: 2¹ and 3¹ → PGCD = **6**
questions.idea: PGCD: the prime must be in EVERY number.

questions.text: Trois horloges sont déréglées. Elles viennent de sonner ensemble. L'une sonne à toutes les **20 minutes**, l'autre à toutes les **15 minutes** et la dernière à toutes les **24 minutes**. Dans combien de minutes sonneront-elles de nouveau ensemble ?
hints: “Ring together AGAIN” — will you use the PPCM or the PGCD?

traps.0: 60 is the PPCM of 20 and 15 — but the 24-minute clock isn't ringing at 60 (60 ÷ 24 = 2.5).
traps.2: 240 is a time they all ring together, but not the FIRST time.
traps.3: 7200 = 20 × 15 × 24. A common multiple, but far from the smallest.

solution: “Again together” = common multiple → the smallest one: PPCM.
questions.idea: “Together again / at the same time” → PPCM.

questions.text:
Julien veut mettre des billes dans de petits sacs. Il possède **48 billes rouges, 64 billes bleues et 112 billes vertes**. Il veut faire le plus grand nombre possible de sacs contenant chacun le même nombre de billes de chaque couleur.
Combien remplit-il de sacs s'il ne reste aucune bille ?
hints: “Same in every bag, nothing left over” → the number of bags must divide 48, 64 AND 112.
“Biggest number of bags” → the biggest such number. PPCM or PGCD?

traps.0: 8 bags works (6, 8, 14 per bag), but it isn't the BIGGEST possible number.
traps.2: 32 doesn't divide 48 (48 ÷ 32 = 1.5), so marbles would be left over.
traps.3: 224 = 48 + 64 + 112 is the total number of marbles.

solution: Number of bags must divide 48, 64 and 112, and we want the greatest → **PGCD**.
questions.idea: “Share equally, biggest number of groups” → PGCD.

questions.text:
Julien fait 16 sacs avec ses 48 billes rouges, 64 bleues et 112 vertes (même nombre de billes de chaque couleur dans chaque sac).
Combien de billes retrouvera-t-on dans chaque sac ?
hints: Work out each colour separately: how many red marbles go in ONE bag?
3 + 4 + 7 — the question asks for the whole bag.

traps.0: 7 is only the green marbles. Add the red and blue ones too.
traps.2: 16 is the number of BAGS, not the marbles in one bag.
traps.3: 224 is every marble in all 16 bags.

questions.idea: Find ONE bag first, then check by scaling back up.

questions.text:
Un travailleur gagne **1200 $** par semaine. Les [[3/10]] de cette somme sont retenus pour les impôts, les [[3/20]] pour la caisse de retraite et le [[1/50]] pour l'assurance-chômage.
Combien reste-t-il à ce travailleur sur une paye de deux semaines ?
hints: Add the three “taken away” fractions first. They need a common denominator — which number do 10, 20 and 50 all divide?
He keeps 1 − [[47/100]] of his pay. Do one week, then double it.

traps.0: 564 $ is what is taken OUT in one week. The question asks what REMAINS.
traps.1: 636 $ is what remains after ONE week. The pay is for two weeks.
traps.2: 1128 $ is what is taken out over two weeks, not what remains.

questions.idea: Common denominator = PPCM of the denominators. Then: total − the parts taken.
